1//! PdfCraft patch (104): an sRGB colour as the process ink that draws back to it through the
2//! CMYK profile pages are drawn with, for an additive colour painted into a `DeviceCMYK`
3//! blending space (ISO 32000-2 §11.3.4).
4//!
5//! Black is `K = 0.4 · k₀² + 0.6 · k₀⁸` with `k₀ = 1 − max(r, g, b)`, light in the mid tones
6//! and full for black; cyan, magenta and yellow are then solved for by Newton's method at that
7//! black, clamped to the ink range. A colour inside the profile's gamut draws as itself; one
8//! outside it lands where the clamped solve stops. The curve matches Acrobat's output for the
9//! greys, black and red measured in a CMYK page group, plain and under a blend mode;
10//! §10.4.2.4's black generation and undercolour removal is for a device without a profile.
11
12use moxcms::{ColorProfile, Layout, TransformF32Executor, TransformOptions};
13use std::cell::Cell;
14use std::sync::{Arc, LazyLock};
15
16use crate::third_party::hayro_interpret::color::CMYK_PROFILE;
17
18/// The weight of `k₀²` in the black ink; the rest is on `k₀⁸`.
19const BLACK_GENERATION: f32 = 0.4;
20/// Newton steps; each costs four profile evaluations.
21const MAX_STEPS: usize = 12;
22/// Close enough: well under one 8-bit level.
23const TOLERANCE: f32 = 0.5 / 255.0;
24/// The finite-difference step for the Jacobian.
25const STEP: f32 = 0.02;
26
27static FORWARD: LazyLock<Option<Arc<TransformF32Executor>>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
28    ColorProfile::new_from_slice(CMYK_PROFILE)
29        .ok()?
30        .create_transform_f32(Layout::Rgba, &ColorProfile::new_srgb(), Layout::Rgb, TransformOptions::default())
31        .ok()
32});
33
34/// The process ink `[C, M, Y, K]` (0 = no ink) that the CMYK profile draws as `rgb`; for a
35/// colour outside its gamut, where the clamped solve stops. `None` when the
36/// profile can't be evaluated or `rgb` isn't finite.
37///
38/// The last colour converted on this thread is kept, as a run of fills (the glyphs of a
39/// line of text) usually shares one colour.
40pub(crate) fn srgb_to_cmyk(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 4]> {
41    if !rgb.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite()) {
42        return None;
43    }
44    let rgb = rgb.map(|v| v.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
45    let key = rgb.map(f32::to_bits);
46    if let Some((last, ink)) = LAST.get()
47        && last == key
48    {
49        return Some(ink);
50    }
51    let ink = solve_ink(rgb)?;
52    LAST.set(Some((key, ink)));
53    Some(ink)
54}
55
56thread_local! {
57    static LAST: Cell<Option<([u32; 3], [f32; 4])>> = const { Cell::new(None) };
58}
59
60fn solve_ink(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 4]> {
61    let forward: &TransformF32Executor = FORWARD.as_ref()?.as_ref();
62    let k0 = 1.0 - rgb[0].max(rgb[1]).max(rgb[2]);
63    let k = BLACK_GENERATION * k0 * k0 + (1.0 - BLACK_GENERATION) * k0.powi(8);
64    let eval = |cmy: [f32; 3]| draw(forward, [cmy[0], cmy[1], cmy[2], k]);
65
66    let mut cmy = rgb.map(|v| 1.0 - v);
67    for _ in 0..MAX_STEPS {
68        let drawn = eval(cmy)?;
69        let residual: [f32; 3] = std::array::from_fn(|i| drawn[i] - rgb[i]);
70        if residual.iter().all(|r| r.abs() < TOLERANCE) {
71            break;
72        }
73        // Column `j` of the Jacobian: how the drawn colour moves with ink `j`.
74        let mut columns = [[0.0_f32; 3]; 3];
75        for (j, column) in columns.iter_mut().enumerate() {
76            let step = if cmy[j] <= 1.0 - STEP { STEP } else { -STEP };
77            let mut moved = cmy;
78            moved[j] += step;
79            let shifted = eval(moved)?;
80            *column = std::array::from_fn(|i| (shifted[i] - drawn[i]) / step);
81        }
82        let Some(delta) = solve(columns, residual.map(|r| -r)) else {
83            break;
84        };
85        cmy = std::array::from_fn(|i| (cmy[i] + delta[i]).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
86    }
87    Some([cmy[0], cmy[1], cmy[2], k])
88}
89
90fn draw(forward: &TransformF32Executor, cmyk: [f32; 4]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
91    let mut out = [0.0_f32; 3];
92    forward.transform(&cmyk, &mut out).ok()?;
93    out.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite()).then_some(out)
94}
95
96/// `x` with `A x = b`, `A` given by its columns (Cramer's rule). `None` when `A` is
97/// singular or the result isn't finite.
98fn solve(a: [[f32; 3]; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
99    let det = |[c0, c1, c2]: [[f32; 3]; 3]| {
100        c0[0] * (c1[1] * c2[2] - c2[1] * c1[2]) - c1[0] * (c0[1] * c2[2] - c2[1] * c0[2]) + c2[0] * (c0[1] * c1[2] - c1[1] * c0[2])
101    };
102    let d = det(a);
103    if !d.is_finite() || d.abs() < 1e-9 {
104        return None;
105    }
106    let x: [f32; 3] = std::array::from_fn(|j| {
107        let mut m = a;
108        m[j] = b;
109        det(m) / d
110    });
111    x.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite()).then_some(x)
112}
